TURN 40 ORG CHART × OKRS
HOW TO READ IT
Every team is a table. Its rows are the lead, its 2026 master-sheet objective, and a people row. Objectives roll up to the FFSA rhythm on the left (Presence, Formation, Mission, Multiplication) plus the year's theme, building with care.
Three kinds of line. OKR lines run from the rhythm to each team objective, coloured by the five progress states. Solid ink is who reports to whom. Dotted is a person serving on two teams.
Clicking lights what's connected and opens the drawer: objective and key results, the OKR Shepherd and monthly update, people, connections. A missing monthly update raises the band, because stuck is not a failure but silence is.
From the 2026 structure document: teams, people, leadership, cross-team service and every objective. Key results and progress numbers are sample data. Caleb holds the Integrator seat. Events, Inside, Outside and Donors have no objective on a master sheet yet.

TURN 36 PRAYER ROOM · PRACTICE
THE RULES
16:00–17:30, Mon · Wed · Thu · Fri. Three 30-minute rows a day. Tuesday is ministry night, so the window is closed and says so.
NIGHT moves to 17:30–20:00. Practice doesn't count toward the 120 hours.
Seven stations, one person each, all on their own ME mix: Drums, Keys, Electric, Cajon, Acoustic, Bass, Vocals. Vocals is one booking, either solo or a group of up to 4.
A full band takes the whole room, and only on an empty row. Only an admin can move people out to make room. Bookings open every Sunday for the coming week, up to 60 minutes each.
36a
A LANE, NOT A SET
The afternoon of the wall, shown larger here. Practice sits in a bone lane between the ordinary sets and NIGHT. Every 30-minute row shows seven squares, one per station in the order drums, keys, electric, cajon, acoustic, bass, vocals. Black means taken. Each row also shows the names. Tuesday's window is hatched shut. A full band is one heavy-bordered block across its rows, with every square filled.

TURN 35 CONTACTS · EVERYONE OUTSIDE THE HUB
WHAT I CHANGED, AND WHY
Contacts and Users stay separate. Contacts is how we reach a person outside the Hub; Users is her profile and login inside it. The profile shows one line when the same person has both, and only to someone allowed to see it — no merging, no shared table.
Person types are retired into labels. You could not remember what a person type was, which is the honest verdict on it: two taxonomies, no rule between them, so they drift into meaning the same thing. Labels absorb the job with one addition — a label is either how she arrived (set once, by the system, never edited) or what she is to us (set by hand). Same table, one flag, and the directory can finally answer "where did all these people come from".
Consent is read, never set here. The ledger in Communications decides whether we may mail her. marketing_status becomes a cache of that ledger, displayed and never edited on this screen — otherwise two screens disagree about the one thing that carries legal weight.
35a
A DIRECTORY THAT ANSWERS IN ONE KEYSTROKE
The search field is the screen, not a control in the corner: it is focused on load, it matches any email or phone a person has ever had rather than the one on file, and it shows what it matched on. Below it, the whole directory as a real table. Labels down the left are the only filter that matters, and the count beside each one is live, so a filtered list is already the audience — it hands straight to Communications instead of being rebuilt there.

WHY THIS ORDER IS SAFE
Paying reserved a kombi-shaped slot, not a kombi. Two paid bookings can sit unassigned for the same week and neither is at risk, because the count would never have sold a third.
34f
WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE CODE
Migrations 103–106 already give you the fleet, bookings, assignments, drivers, inspections, agreements, PayFast payments and per-vehicle Xero codes. What you have is an internal request-and-approve queue that books a named vehicle and takes payment later. What you described is a public shop that sells a class of vehicle, takes the money before it commits anything, and leaves the choice of vehicle to Gideon. These are the deltas.
ALREADY THERE — DO NOT REBUILD
vehicles · the six plates, seats, fuel, colour, xero_item_code
Seeded from the booking sheet. Status already covers maintenance and retired.
vehicle_booking_assignments + getOverlappingAssignments
This is the availability engine the public form needs. It works today.
vehicle_inspections · mileage, fuel_full, washed, damage_panels, inventory
Both sign-out and sign-in, with a private bucket for damage photos and licences.
vehicle_agreements · the signed usage policy
Already per booking. Only the ordering changes: signed before the card, not after.
vehicle_payments + PayFast ITN + Xero posting
markVehiclePaymentPaidIfPending → markBookingPaid → Xero, keyed on the vehicle's item code. The webhook is the right place to confirm a booking.

THE ONE RULE THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST
A hold is not a booking and a booking is not a paid booking. Only the PayFast webhook — or an accepted coupon — may move a booking to confirmed. Nothing in the browser gets to decide that a vehicle is reserved.

TURN 7 PRAYER ROOM · 6A + HAPPENING NOW · 30-MINUTE SLOTS
6a's week of columns with 6b's happening-now rail attached. The 30-minute problem is solved by dropping the fixed hour grid: every block is drawn to its real length on a time axis, so a 14:30–15:30 set is simply a block that starts halfway down the 14:00 row. Nothing has to round to the hour, and short slots stay legible because they shrink rather than getting their own row. Your three key times — 08:00–09:30, 12:00–14:00, 17:00–19:00 — are marked down the whole wall so the eye finds them first. 7b shows the other way to do it if you'd rather read one day at a time.
7a
WEEK ON A TIME AXIS
Blocks are sized by duration, so half-hour slots read as half-height and never need their own grid row. Key times carry a marked band across all seven days. Overnight collapses to one strip per day since it's rarely the thing you're scanning for.
JV
